components.name: Mesh From Surface
components.info: Create a triangular mesh from a surface.

inputs.name: Grid min count
inputs.info: The minimal grid count in the initial quad mesh

inputs.name: Grid max count
inputs.info: The maximal grid count in the initial quad mesh

outputs.name: Meshes
outputs.info: The mesh or meshes obtained by the default Rhino mesher.

components.author: DavidR
components.name: Mesh From Constraints
components.info: Construct a constrained tesselation out of points and optional boundaries.

inputs.name: Plane
inputs.info: Optional override for tesselation plane. If omitted, the best fit plane is used.

inputs.name: Balance
inputs.info: Insert additional vertices to balance the output mesh.

inputs.name: Constraints
inputs.info: Optional tesselation constraints such as boundaries, holes and hard edges. These must be created using dedicated components.

components.author: DavidR
components.name: Mesh From Edges
components.info: Create a mesh out of a collection of potential edge lines.

inputs.name: Valence
inputs.info: Allowed facet valence, i.e. the maximum number of allowed edges per facet.

outputs.name: Mesh
outputs.info: Mesh constructed from edges which were part of closed loops.

outputs.name: Shortfall
outputs.info: Number of lines, which did not become mesh edges.

components.author: DavidR
components.name: Mesh From Grid
components.info: Create a mesh out of multiple rows of points.

inputs.name: Points
inputs.info: Sequential rows of points. When the number of points in a subsequent row changes, a new grid is started. When the penultimate integer in the tree path of a point list changes, this also signals the start of a new grid.

inputs.name: Close U
inputs.info: Open or close the mesh in the U direction.

inputs.name: Close V
inputs.info: Open or close the mesh in the V direction.

outputs.name: Paths
outputs.info: Ranges of paths that were used to create each mesh.

components.author: DavidR
components.name: Mesh From Points
components.info: Create a mesh by tesselating a collection of points, using a Delaunay triangulation algorithm.

inputs.name: Space
inputs.info: Optional underlying space in which to perform tesselation.

outputs.name: Mesh
outputs.info: Delaunay-compliant mesh with vertices at all non-coincident points.

components.author: DavidR
components.name: Mesh Patch
components.info: Create a mesh out of boundary and hole curves, with optional points.

inputs.name: Curves
inputs.info: Boundary curves for the patch. Curves inside other curves will automatically be treated as hole boundaries.

inputs.name: Edges
inputs.info: Optional interior edge constraints for patch.

outputs.name: Mesh
outputs.info: Mesh coincident with boundaries, points and edges.

components.author: DavidR
components.name: Mesh Pipe
components.info: Create a tube-shaped mesh with a specified number of facets.

inputs.name: Segments
inputs.info: Number of facets around the pipe.

inputs.name: Accuracy
inputs.info: Value regulating the number of facets along the curve (0 = fewest facets, 1 = most facets) .

inputs.name: Cap Type
inputs.info: Type of cap at each discontinuity along the curve.

components.author: DavidR
components.name: Mesh From UV
components.info: Create a discrete mesh approximation of a surface.

inputs.name: Tolerance
inputs.info: Optional absolute tolerance to use during approximation.

inputs.name: Planes
inputs.info: If true, nice planar surfaces will result in the simplest possible meshes.

inputs.name: Jagged
inputs.info: If true, meshes belonging to different surface faces will not be stitched together along edges.

inputs.name: Precise
inputs.info: If true, the mesh vertices will use high precision coordinates.

inputs.name: Repair
inputs.info: If true, attempts will be made to close the mesh if it isn't yet but should be.

inputs.name: Minimum Edge
inputs.info: Optional minimum allowed edge length. This places a lower limit on the subdivision density.

inputs.name: Maximum Edge
inputs.info: Optional maximum allowed edge length. This places limits on the allowed size of long mesh edges.

inputs.name: Refine Grid
inputs.info: If true, the initial sampling grid can be refined to better fit local conditions.

inputs.name: Minimum Grid
inputs.info: Optional minimum number of quads in the initial sampling grid.

inputs.name: Maximum Grid
inputs.info: Optional maximum number of quads in the initial sampling grid.

inputs.name: Grid Aspect
inputs.info: Optional limits on the aspect ratio of quads in the initial sampling grid.

components.author: DavidR
components.name: Polyline Constraint
components.info: Create a tesselation constraint which connects point coordinates.

components.author: DavidR
components.name: Subdivide Mesh
components.info: Apply a subdivision scheme to an existing mesh.

inputs.name: Steps
inputs.info: Number of subdivision steps. Each additional step approximately quadruples the number of facets in a mesh.

inputs.name: Retain Creases
inputs.info: Retain the unwelded creases in the input mesh.

inputs.name: Retain Corners
inputs.info: Specify the angle, above which convex corners of the input mesh boundary will be retained.

components.author: DavidR
components.name: Voronoi Cells
components.info: Construct the 2D voronoi cell boundaries for a collection of points.

inputs.name: Plane
inputs.info: Optional plane override. If omitted, the best fit plane is used.

inputs.name: Extend
inputs.info: Extension length of cell boundaries going off to infinity.

components.author: DavidR
components.name: Voronoi Edges
components.info: Construct the 2D voronoi edges for a collection of points.

inputs.name: Plane
inputs.info: Optional plane override. If omitted, the best fit plane is used.

inputs.name: Extend
inputs.info: Extension length of voronoi edges going off to infinity.

components.author: DavidR
components.name: Voronoi On Surface
components.info: Construct a Voronoi tesselation within the UV space of a surface.

components.author: MathiasF
components.name: Weighted Voronoi
components.info: Construct the 2D Voronoi diagram of points with additive and multiplicative weights.

inputs.name: Points
inputs.info: Site points, in the XY plane.

inputs.name: Multiplicative
inputs.info: Optional multiplicative weight per point (positive). If omitted, all weights are 1.

inputs.name: Additive
inputs.info: Optional additive weight per point. If omitted, all weights are 0.

inputs.name: Blend
inputs.info: 0 for a purely additive diagram, 1 for a purely multiplicative one.

inputs.name: Boundary
inputs.info: Optional clipping rectangle. If omitted, the points' bounding box grown by a quarter is used.

outputs.name: Left
outputs.info: Index of the site on the left of each edge, -1 for the outside.

outputs.name: Right
outputs.info: Index of the site on the right of each edge, -1 for the outside.

outputs.name: Cells
outputs.info: Closed cell boundaries. A cell with holes gives several loops, holes run clockwise.

outputs.name: Cell Index
outputs.info: Index of the site of each cell loop.

components.author: DanPiker
components.name: Align Vertices
components.info: Snap together mesh vertices which are closer than a specified distance.

inputs.name: Mesh
inputs.info: Mesh or meshes whose vertices to align.

inputs.name: Distance
inputs.info: Distance within which to align vertices.

inputs.name: Naked Only
inputs.info: If true, only naked vertices will be aligned.

outputs.name: Mesh
outputs.info: Mesh or meshes with vertices aligned.

components.author: DanPiker
components.name: Blur Mesh
components.info: Blur the vertex colours of a mesh.

inputs.name: Fixed Vertices
inputs.info: Indices of vertices which should keep their colour fixed during blurring.

inputs.name: Iterations
inputs.info: Number of blurring iterations to perform.

components.author: DavidR
components.name: Clothe Naked Edges
components.info: Attempt to clothe all naked edges in a mesh either by slightly moving nearby vertices together, or by splitting edges located near naked vertices.

inputs.name: Mesh
inputs.info: Mesh with naked edges to fix.

outputs.name: Result
outputs.info: True if naked edges were fixed.

components.author: DavidR
components.name: Collapse Facets
components.info: Collapse mesh facets whose indices are included in a given list.

components.author: DavidR
components.name: Collapse Indicated Facets
components.info: Collapse facets in a mesh using a list of booleans.

inputs.name: Map
inputs.info: Boolean list indicating whether to collapse individual facets.

components.author: DavidR
components.name: Collapse Particular Facets
components.info: Collapse mesh facets whose properties exceed given threshold values.

inputs.name: Area
inputs.info: Optional area limit. Facets with areas smaller than this limit will be collapsed.

inputs.name: Aspect
inputs.info: Optional aspect ratio limit. Facets with aspect ratios less than this limit will be collapsed.

inputs.name: Edge Length
inputs.info: Optional edge length limit. Facets with edges whose lengths are smaller than this limit will be collapsed.

components.author: DanPiker
components.name: Cull Facets
components.info: Remove mesh facets indicated by a boolean pattern.

inputs.name: Pattern
inputs.info: Culling pattern. Faces paired up with the value `false` in the pattern are retained, while those paired up with the value `true` are culled.

components.author: DanPiker
components.name: Cull Vertices
components.info: Remove mesh vertices indicated by a boolean pattern.

inputs.name: Pattern
inputs.info: Culling pattern. Vertices paired up with the value `false` in the pattern are retained, while those paired up with the value `true` are culled.

inputs.name: Shrink
inputs.info: Shrink affected quads to triangles if possible.

components.author: DavidR
components.name: Delete Facets
components.info: Delete mesh facets whose indices are included in a given list.

components.author: DavidR
components.name: Delete Particular Facets
components.info: Delete all mesh facets whose properties exceed various threshold values.

inputs.name: Area
inputs.info: Optional area limit. Facets with areas smaller than this will be deleted.

inputs.name: Aspect
inputs.info: Optional aspect ratio limit. Facets with aspect ratios less than this will be deleted.

inputs.name: Edge Length
inputs.info: Optional edge length limit. Facets whose shortest edge is smaller than this value will be deleted.

components.author: DavidR
components.name: Delete Vertices
components.info: Delete mesh vertices whose indices are included in a given list.

components.author: DavidR
components.name: Fill Mesh Holes
components.info: Attempt to patch all holes in a mesh by triangulating loops of naked edges.

outputs.name: Mesh
outputs.info: Mesh with, hopefully fewer, ideally no holes.

components.author: DanP
components.name: Flip Mesh
components.info: Flip the normal directions of a mesh.

inputs.name: Vertex Normals
inputs.info: If true, flip the vertex normal directions.

inputs.name: Facet Normals
inputs.info: If true, flip the facet normal directions.

inputs.name: Facet Orientations
inputs.info: If true, reverse the facet orientations.

inputs.name: Ngon Directions
inputs.info: If true, reverse the boundary directions of n-gons.

components.author: DavidR
components.name: Join Meshes
components.info: Join several meshes into a single mesh.

inputs.name: Merge Vertices
inputs.info: Merge coincident vertices in the joined mesh.

inputs.name: Match Edges
inputs.info: Match edges in the joined mesh.

components.author: DavidR
components.name: Match Mesh Edges
components.info: Move the vertices and split the edges of a mesh until adjacent naked edges become coincident.

inputs.name: Mesh
inputs.info: Mesh with naked edges to match.

outputs.name: Result
outputs.info: True if any edges were matched.

components.author: DavidR
components.name: Merge Coplanar Facets
components.info: Merge contiguous coplanar mesh facets into single n-gons.

inputs.name: Allow Holes
inputs.info: Allow the creation of n-gons with holes.

components.author: MathiasF
components.name: Mesh Split Plane
components.info: Split a mesh with an infinite plane.

outputs.name: Above
outputs.info: Mesh fragments on the positive side of the plane.

outputs.name: Below
outputs.info: Mesh fragments on the negative side of the plane.

outputs.name: Sections
outputs.info: Cut polylines where the plane intersects the mesh.

components.author: DavidR
components.name: Move Mesh Vertices
components.info: Move vertices of an existing mesh using per-vertex motion vectors.

inputs.name: Recompute Normals
inputs.info: Recompute the mesh normals to reflect the change in shape.

components.author: DavidR
components.name: Offset Mesh
components.info: Offset the vertices of a mesh along their normal directions.

inputs.name: Offset Distance
inputs.info: Offset distance. Positive values indicate the offset is in the direction of the normal.

inputs.name: Solidify
inputs.info: Specifies whether the offset mesh and the original mesh are stitched together along their naked edges.

inputs.name: Average Normals
inputs.info: Specifies whether to average the normals along creases prior to offsetting.

components.author: DavidR
components.name: Pull Mesh Vertices
components.info: Pull mesh vertices onto nearby shapes.

inputs.name: Falloff
inputs.info: Distance threshold for the pulling operation as a number, or a falloff function based on distance.

inputs.name: Vertex Filter
inputs.info: Types of vertices to be included.

components.author: DavidR
components.name: Quad Remesh
components.info: Create a new quad mesh based on an existing shape.

inputs.name: Shape
inputs.info: Base shape. Must be either a mesh or a surface.

inputs.name: Target Count
inputs.info: Optional target quad count. When unset, the 'Target Length' will be used instead.

inputs.name: Target Length
inputs.info: Optional target edge length. When unset, the 'Target Count' will be used instead.

inputs.name: Adaptive Size
inputs.info: A number between zero and one hundred controlling how quad sizes change depending on curvature.

inputs.name: Adaptive Count
inputs.info: If true, allows high curvature areas to affect the target quad count.

inputs.name: Maintain Edges
inputs.info: Specifies how surface edges are maintained during remeshing.

inputs.name: Maintain Creases
inputs.info: If true, sharp creases in the underlying surface are maintained.

inputs.name: Guide Curves
inputs.info: Optional guide curves for local remeshing directions.

inputs.name: Symmetry
inputs.info: Symmetry axis to apply during remeshing.

components.author: DavidR
components.name: Quad Remesh
components.info: Create a new quad mesh based on an existing shape.

inputs.name: Shape
inputs.info: Base shape. Must be either a mesh or a surface.

inputs.name: Options
inputs.info: Quad remeshing options. These can be created using a dedicated component.

inputs.name: Guides
inputs.info: Optional guide curves for local remeshing directions.

components.author: DavidR
components.name: Quad Remesh Options
components.info: Create settings used for quad remesh operations.

inputs.name: Target Count
inputs.info: Target quad count. When unset, the 'Target Length' will be used instead.

inputs.name: Target Length
inputs.info: Target edge length. When unset, the 'Target Count' will be used instead.

inputs.name: Adaptive Size
inputs.info: A number between zero and one hundred controlling how quad sizes change depending on curvature.

inputs.name: Adaptive Count
inputs.info: Specifies whether high curvature areas are allowed to affect the target quad count.

inputs.name: Maintain Edges
inputs.info: Specifies how surface edges are maintained during remeshing.

inputs.name: Maintain Creases
inputs.info: Specifies whether sharp creases are maintained.

inputs.name: Symmetry
inputs.info: Symmetry axis to apply during remeshing.

components.author: DavidR
components.name: Rebuild Mesh Normals
components.info: Reconstruct all vertex and facet normals based on the shape of the mesh.

components.author: DavidR
components.name: Reduce Mesh
components.info: Reduce the facet count of a mesh by merging smaller facets into larger ones.

inputs.name: Allow Distortion
inputs.info: Specifies whether the mesh shape may be distorted.

components.author: DavidR
components.name: Remesh
components.info: Create a new mesh based on the shape of an existing one.

inputs.name: Target Count
inputs.info: Target facet count. High curvature areas in the mesh may cause the remesher to veer away from the target.

components.author: DavidR
components.name: Retopologise Facets
components.info: Triangulate or quadrangulate mesh facets.

components.author: DavidR
components.name: Mesh Colours
components.info: Set the vertex colours of an existing mesh.

components.author: DavidR
components.name: Mesh Colours From Numbers
components.info: Colour the vertices of a mesh by evaluating a given gradient.

inputs.name: Numbers
inputs.info: List of numbers encoding the value of each vertex.

inputs.name: Scaling Method
inputs.info: Scaling method for stretching the gradient to the number distribution.

components.author: DavidR
components.name: Mesh Colours From Field
components.info: Set the vertex colours of an existing mesh, using a scalar field and a gradient.

inputs.name: Field
inputs.info: Scalar field for computing gradient parameters per vertex.

components.author: DavidR
components.name: Set Mesh Normals
components.info: Set the vertex normals of an existing mesh.

components.author: DavidR
components.name: Set Mesh Vertices
components.info: Change the vertex locations of an existing mesh.

inputs.name: Recompute Normals
inputs.info: Recompute the normals of the mesh to reflect the change in shape.

components.author: DanP
components.name: Shrinkwrap
components.info: Shrinkwrap geometry with a mesh.

inputs.name: Offset
inputs.info: Inwards or outwards offset distance of the wrap.

inputs.name: Smoothing
inputs.info: Number of smoothing iterations to perform.

inputs.name: Optimisation
inputs.info: Polygon optimisation factor between 0 and 1. Lower values give better feature preservation at the cost of a higher facet count.

inputs.name: Fill Holes
inputs.info: If true, holes in the input are filled before wrapping.

inputs.name: Edge Length
inputs.info: Optional target edge length for wrapping mesh. If omitted, a fraction of the bounding box is used.

inputs.name: Meshing Density
inputs.info: Meshing density factor between 0 and 1 to use when meshing input surfaces.

components.author: DavidR
components.name: Smooth Mesh
components.info: Smooth an existing mesh by moving vertices towards the averaged out locations of their neighbours.

inputs.name: Strength
inputs.info: Smoothing strength as a factor between zero for no smoothing, and one for full smoothing.

inputs.name: Limit
inputs.info: Optional limit for how far vertices may move.

inputs.name: Clamp Naked Edges
inputs.info: Clamp vertices on naked edges in place.

inputs.name: Clamp Creases
inputs.info: Clamp vertices on unwelded edges in place.

inputs.name: Iterations
inputs.info: Number of times to apply the smoothing process.

components.author: DavidR
components.name: Split Disjoint Meshes
components.info: Split a single mesh into its disjoint component parts.

components.author: DavidR
components.name: Split Unwelded Meshes
components.info: Split a single mesh into its unwelded component parts.

components.author: DanP
components.name: Tri Remesh
components.info: Create a triangular mesh with improved triangle quality from an input geometry.

inputs.name: Start Geometry
inputs.info: The starting geometry to remesh. Can be a mesh or a surface.

inputs.name: Sharp
inputs.info: If true, sharp creases and corners will be preserved.

inputs.name: Feature Curves
inputs.info: Optional curves to preserve as edges.

inputs.name: Feature Points
inputs.info: Optional points to preserve as vertices.

inputs.name: Target Edge Length
inputs.info: Optional target edge length. If omitted, 1/30th of the diagonal of the shape bounding box is used.

inputs.name: Iterations
inputs.info: Maximum number of iterations to run the remeshing process if not converged.

outputs.name: Feature Edges
outputs.info: Edge lines preserved in the remeshing process.

components.author: DavidR
components.name: Unify Mesh Normals
components.info: Fix mesh normal inconsistencies caused by facet winding orientations.

inputs.name: Unify Facets
inputs.info: Unify facet normals and winding orientations based on the surrounding facets.

inputs.name: Unify Vertices
inputs.info: Unify vertex normals based on the surrounding facet normals.

components.author: DavidR
components.name: Unweld Mesh
components.info: Unweld all mesh edges whose adjacent facets form an angle sharper than a given threshold.

inputs.name: Unwelding Angle
inputs.info: Unweld angle. All edges whose adjacent facets form an angle sharper than this threshold will be unwelded.

components.author: DavidR
components.name: Warp Mesh Normals
components.info: Assign vertex normals from a vector field to an existing mesh.

components.author: DavidR
components.name: Warp Mesh Vertices
components.info: Move the vertices of an existing mesh using a vector field.

inputs.name: Recompute Normals
inputs.info: Specifies whether to recompute the normals of the mesh to reflect the change in shape.

components.author: DavidR
components.name: Weld Mesh
components.info: Weld all edges in a mesh whose adjacent facets form an angle exceeding a given threshold.

inputs.name: Welding Angle
inputs.info: All edges whose adjacent facets form an angle larger than this threshold will be welded.

components.author: DavidR
components.name: Shear From Angles
components.info: Create a shearing transformation based on X and Y angles. If an input shape is provided, it will be sheared accordingly.

inputs.name: Plane
inputs.info: Shearing base plane. Geometry within this plane does not get transformed.

inputs.name: X Angle
inputs.info: Shearing angle around the plane X-axis.

inputs.name: Y Angle
inputs.info: Shearing angle around the plane Y-axis.

inputs.name: Maintain Height
inputs.info: If true, the shearing magnitude is adjusted to maintain elevations.

components.author: DavidR
components.name: Shear From Normal
components.info: Creating a shearing transformation towards a custom direction. If an input shape is provided, it will be sheared accordingly.

inputs.name: Plane
inputs.info: Shearing base plane. Geometry within this plane does not get transformed.

components.author: DavidR
components.name: Classify Transform
components.info: Classify a transformation based on its mathematical category.

outputs.name: Identity
outputs.info: True if the transformation equals the identity matrix and does not affect shapes at all.

outputs.name: Translation
outputs.info: True if the transformation contains only translations.

outputs.name: Rotation
outputs.info: True if the transformation contains only rotations.

outputs.name: Rigid
outputs.info: True if the transformation is made up of a combination of translations and rotations.

outputs.name: Similarity
outputs.info: True if the transformation is made up of a combination of translations, rotations, dilations and reflections.

outputs.name: Affine
outputs.info: True if the transformation is affine, meaning it lacks perspective or tapering aspects.

components.author: DavidR
components.name: Decompose Affine
components.info: Decompose an affine transformation into a linear and a translational aspect.

outputs.name: Translation
outputs.info: Translational aspect of the given transformation.

outputs.name: Linear
outputs.info: Linear aspect of the given transformation.

components.author: DavidR
components.name: Decompose Rigid
components.info: Decompose a rigid transformation into a translational and a rotational aspect.

outputs.name: Translation
outputs.info: Translational aspect of the given transformation.

outputs.name: Rotation
outputs.info: Rotational aspect of the given transformation.

components.author: DavidR
components.name: Decompose Similarity
components.info: Decompose a similarity transformation into a translation, a dilation and a rotational aspect.

outputs.name: Translation
outputs.info: Translational aspect of the given transformation.

outputs.name: Dilation
outputs.info: Dilational aspect of the given transformation.

outputs.name: Rotation
outputs.info: Rotational aspect of the given transformation.

components.author: DavidR
components.name: Dilation Vector
components.info: Extract the dilation vector of a transformation matrix, corrected for rotation.

outputs.name: X Factor
outputs.info: Scaling factor for the X direction.

outputs.name: Y Factor
outputs.info: Scaling factor for the Y direction.

outputs.name: Z Factor
outputs.info: Scaling factor for the Z direction.

components.author: DavidR
components.name: Extract Dilation
components.info: Extract the dilational aspect of a transformation.

outputs.name: Pivot
outputs.info: Origin point of the embedded dilation.

outputs.name: Factor
outputs.info: Scaling factor of the embedded dilation.

components.author: DavidR
components.name: Extract Rotation
components.info: Extract the axis and the angle of a rotational transformation.

components.author: DavidR
components.name: Extract Translation
components.info: Extract the translational aspect of a transformation.

outputs.name: Translation
outputs.info: Translation embedded in the given transformation.

components.author: DavidR
components.name: Extract Yaw-Pitch-Roll
components.info: Extract the yaw, pitch and roll angles of a transformation.

outputs.name: Yaw
outputs.info: Yaw rotation embedded in the transformation.

outputs.name: Pitch
outputs.info: Pitch rotation embedded in the transformation.

outputs.name: Roll
outputs.info: Roll rotation embedded in the transformation.

components.author: DavidR
components.name: Translation Vector
components.info: Extract the translation vector of a transformation matrix. Note that rotation and dilation will manifest as a kind of translation too, but are not included in these outputs.

outputs.name: X Motion
outputs.info: Translation motion in the X direction.

outputs.name: Y Motion
outputs.info: Translation motion in the Y direction.

outputs.name: Z Motion
outputs.info: Translation motion in the Z direction.

components.author: DavidR
components.name: Classify Quaternion
components.info: Classify a quaternion by its properties.

outputs.info: If true, the quaternion is valid.

outputs.name: Scalar
outputs.info: If true, the scalar coefficient is non-zero, while all vector coefficients equal zero.

outputs.name: Vector
outputs.info: If true, at least one of the vector coefficients is not zero.

outputs.name: Unit

components.info: Dissect a quaternion by extracting the A, B, C, and D coefficients.

components.author: DavidR
components.name: Quaternion Standard
components.info: Create a quaternion standard value.

components.author: DavidR

components.info: Compute the norm-distance between two quaternions.

outputs.name: Distance
outputs.info: Norm-distance between the two given quaternions.

components.author: DavidR
components.name: Quaternion From Coefficients
components.info: Create a quaternion out of A, B, C, and D coefficients.

components.author: DavidR
components.name: Quaternion From Orientation
components.info: Create the quaternion needed to rotate from a source to a target plane.

outputs.name: Quaternion

components.author: DavidR
components.name: Quaternion From Rotation
components.info: Convert an axial rotation into an equivalent quaternion.

components.author: DavidR
components.name: Rotate Towards
components.info: Rotate one quaternion towards another.

components.author: DavidR
components.name: Rotation From Quaternion
components.info: Convert a quaternion into an equivalent axial rotation.

outputs.name: Axis
outputs.info: Rotation axis, anchored at the world origin.

components.author: DavidR
components.name: Quaternion Slerp
components.info: Interpolate between two quaternions using spherical-linear interpolation.

components.info: Create a twisted box cage with straight edges out of eight corner points.

outputs.name: Cage
outputs.info: Twisted box cage with straight edges.

components.info: Combine multiple transformations into a single one.

components.author: DavidR
components.name: Invert Transformation
components.info: Create the inverse of a transformation, when possible.

inputs.info: Transformation to invert. This transformation must not involve projections onto planes, lines or points.

components.author: DavidR

components.info: Fully repeat a transformation a given number of times.

components.info: Transform a shape and its meta data with a given transformation.

components.author: DavidR

components.author: DavidR

components.author: DavidR
components.name: Camera Obscura
components.info: Invert a shape through the pinhole point of a camera obscura. If an input shape is provided, it will be transformed accordingly.

inputs.name: Factor
inputs.info: Scaling factor for the inverted projection.

components.author: DavidR
components.name: Mirror
components.info: Create a reflection transformation in a plane. If an input shape is provided, it will be transformed accordingly.

components.author: DavidR
components.name: Project
components.info: Create a projection transformation onto a plane.If an input shape is provided, it will be transformed accordingly.

components.author: DavidR
components.name: Project Along
components.info: Create a projection transformation onto a plane along a given direction. If an input shape is provided, it will be transformed accordingly.

inputs.name: Direction
inputs.info: Projection direction. Must not be parallel to the plane.

components.author: DavidR
components.name: Rectangle Mapping
components.info: Transform a shape using source and target reference rectangles. The specifics of the transformation are encoded by the differences between the rectangles.

outputs.name: Transformation
outputs.info: Transformation consisting of the translation, dilation and rotation required to go from the source to the target rectangle.

components.author: DavidR
components.name: Scale 1D
components.info: Create a dilation, or scaling transformation, in a single direction. If an input shape is provided, it will be scaled accordingly.

inputs.name: Factor
inputs.info: Scaling factor along the axis, pinned at the axis start point.

components.author: DavidR
components.name: Scale 2D
components.info: Create two-dimensional dilation, or scaling transformation. If an input shape is provided, it will be scaled accordingly.

inputs.name: Factor
inputs.info: Uniform scaling factor in the origin plane X and Y directions.

components.author: DavidR
components.name: Scale 3D
components.info: Create a dilation, or scaling transformation, which is equal in all directions. If an input shape is provided, it will be scaled accordingly.

inputs.name: Factor
inputs.info: Uniform scaling factor towards or away from the origin.

components.author: DavidR
components.name: Scale Non-uniform
components.info: Create a dilation, or scaling transformation, using different factors in the X, Y, and Z directions. If an input shape is provided, it will be scaled accordingly.

inputs.name: Plane
inputs.info: Plane specifying the origin and axis directions of the scaling transformation.

inputs.name: Factor X
inputs.info: Scaling factor in plane X direction.

inputs.name: Factor Y
inputs.info: Scaling factor in plane Y direction.

inputs.name: Factor Z
inputs.info: Scaling factor in plane Z direction.

components.author: DavidR
components.name: Scale To Area
components.info: Resize a shape equally in all directions until its area falls within an allowed range. This component assumes the area of a shape changes with the square of the scaling factor.

components.author: DavidR
components.name: Scale To Volume
components.info: Resize a shape equally in all directions until its volume falls within an allowed range. This component assumes the volume of a shape changes with the cube of the scaling factor.

components.author: DanP
components.name: Tetrahedron Mapping
components.info: Transform a shape using source and target reference tetrahedra. The specifics of the transformation are encoded by the differences between the tetrahedra.

inputs.name: Source
inputs.info: The four vertices of the tetrahedron representing the initial state.

inputs.name: Target
inputs.info: The four vertices of the tetrahedron representing the final state.

outputs.name: Transformation
outputs.info: Transformation consisting of the translation, dilation, rotation and shearing required to go from the source to the target tetrahedron.

components.author: DavidR
components.name: Triangle Mapping
components.info: Transform a shape using source and target reference triangles. The specifics of the transformation are encoded by the differences between the triangles.

outputs.name: Transformation
outputs.info: Transformation consisting of the translation, dilation, rotation and shearing required to go from the source to the target triangle.

components.author: DavidR
components.name: Array Linear
components.info: Create a linear array of translations. If an input shape is provided, it will be transformed accordingly.

inputs.name: Motion
inputs.info: Motion vector describing the spacing between adjacent array elements.

outputs.name: Transformations
outputs.info: List of translations applied to each element in the array.

components.author: DavidR
components.name: Array Rectangular
components.info: Create a rectangular array of translations. If an input shape is provided, it will be transformed accordingly.

inputs.name: Cell
inputs.info: Grid cell describing the spacing between adjacent array elements.

inputs.name: Range X
inputs.info: Number of array elements in the cell X direction.

inputs.name: Range Y
inputs.info: Number of array elements in the cell Y direction.

outputs.name: Transformations
outputs.info: List of translations applied to each element in the array.

components.author: DavidR
components.name: Array Boxular
components.info: Create a volumetric, orthogonal array of translations. If an input shape is provided, it will be transformed accordingly.

inputs.name: Cell
inputs.info: Grid cell describing the spacing between adjacent array elements.

inputs.name: Range X
inputs.info: Number of array elements in the cell X direction.

inputs.name: Range Y
inputs.info: Number of array elements in the cell Y direction.

inputs.name: Range Z
inputs.info: Number of array elements in the cell Z direction.

outputs.name: Transformations
outputs.info: List of translations applied to each element in the array.

components.author: DavidR
components.name: Array Along Curve
components.info: Create an array of transformations along a rail curve. If an input shape is provided, it will be transformed accordingly.

inputs.name: Count
inputs.info: Number of transformed elements along the curve.

inputs.name: Orientation
inputs.info: Orientation constraint for the arrayed shapes.

outputs.name: Transformations
outputs.info: List of transformations applied to each element in the array.

components.author: DavidR
components.name: Array Arcular
components.info: Create an arc shaped array of rotations spanning a sweep angle. If an input shape is provided, it will be transformed accordingly.

inputs.name: Plane
inputs.info: Centre and orientation of the array.

inputs.name: Angle
inputs.info: Sweep angle of the array, measured counter-clockwise from the plane x-axis.

inputs.name: Count
inputs.info: Number of elements in the array.

inputs.name: Extent
inputs.info: Rule for how the sweep is filled with elements.

outputs.name: Transformations
outputs.info: List of rotations applied to each element in the array.

components.author: DavidR
components.name: Array Circular
components.info: Create a circular array of rotations. If an input shape is provided, it will be transformed accordingly.

inputs.name: Plane
inputs.info: Centre and orientation of circular array.

inputs.name: Count
inputs.info: Number of elements in the array.

outputs.name: Transformations
outputs.info: List of rotations applied to each element in the array.

components.author: DavidR
components.name: Array From Gaps
components.info: Create a sequence of shapes along a curve with a specific gap size. If an input shape is provided, it will be transformed accordingly.

components.author: DavidR
components.name: Array Polar
components.info: Create a polar array of rotations. If an input shape is provided, it will be transformed accordingly.

inputs.name: Plane
inputs.info: Centre and orientation of polar array.

inputs.name: Elevation
inputs.info: Optional function giving the elevation of each array element. The function must be scaled to element index, rather than element angle.

outputs.name: Transformations
outputs.info: List of transformations applied to each element in the array.

components.author: DavidR
components.name: Move
components.info: Create a translation transformation along a vector. If an input shape is provided, it will be transformed accordingly.

components.author: DavidR
components.name: Move Onto Plane
components.info: Move a shape in a direction perpendicular to a plane, until the plane and shape come into contact.

inputs.name: Above
inputs.info: If true, move objects above the plane.

inputs.name: Below
inputs.info: If true, move objects below the plane.

components.author: DavidR
components.name: Move Polar
components.info: Create a translation transformation using polar coordinates. If an input shape is provided, it will be transformed accordingly.

components.author: DavidR
components.name: Move With Field
components.info: Move a shape using the flow of a vector field, as measured at the centre of the shape bounding box.

inputs.name: Field
inputs.info: Field exerting a force on the shape.

inputs.name: Strength
inputs.info: Motion strength. Single Step scales the field vector by it, Integrate reads it as the duration of the flow, and Trajectory reads it as the length of the trajectory. Negative values move the shape upstream.

components.author: DavidR
components.name: Move With Field
components.info: Move a shape using the direction and magnitude of a vector field, as measured at the centre of the shape bounding box.

inputs.name: Field
inputs.info: Field exerting a force on the shape.

components.author: DavidR
components.name: Orient
components.info: Create an orientation transformation from one plane to another. An orientation consists of translational and rotational aspects. If an input shape is provided, it will be transformed accordingly.

components.author: DavidR
components.name: Orient 2D
components.info: Create an orientation transformation from one axis to another. A two-dimensional orientation consists of translational, rotational, and dilational aspects. If an input shape is provided, it will be transformed accordingly.

components.author: DavidR
components.name: Orient Direction
components.info: Create an orientation transformation from one direction to another in 3D space.

components.author: DavidR
components.name: Rotate About Axis
components.info: Create a rotation around an origin point and an axis direction. If an input shape is provided, it will be rotated accordingly.

inputs.name: Angle
inputs.info: Rotational angle. Positive angles cause a counter-clockwise rotation.

components.author: DavidR
components.name: Rotate Direction
components.info: Create a rotation from one direction to another. If an input shape is provided, it will be rotated accordingly.

components.author: DavidR
components.name: Rotate Euler Angles
components.info: Create a rotation through Euler angles.

inputs.name: Alpha
inputs.info: First rotation about the world Z axis.

inputs.name: Beta
inputs.info: Second rotation about the world Y axis.

inputs.name: Gamma
inputs.info: Third rotation about the world Z axis again.

components.author: DavidR
components.name: Rotate In Plane
components.info: Create a rotation around the origin and the normal axis of a plane. If an input shape is provided, it will be rotated accordingly.

inputs.name: Angle
inputs.info: Rotational angle. Positive angles cause a counter-clockwise rotation.

components.author: DavidR
components.name: Yaw Pitch Roll
components.info: Create a rotation through Tait-Bryan angles, commonly known as Yaw, Pitch, and Roll.

inputs.name: Yaw
inputs.info: Yaw rotation about the world Z axis.

inputs.name: Pitch
inputs.info: Pitch rotation about the world Y axis.

inputs.name: Roll
inputs.info: Roll rotation about the world X axis.

components.author: DavidR
components.name: Apply Deform
components.info: Apply a non-linear spatial deformation to a shape.

inputs.name: Preserve
inputs.info: If true, the underlying control-point structure is preserved during deformation.

components.author: DavidR
components.name: Bend Deform
components.info: Create a bending deformation. If an input shape is provided, it will be deformed accordingly.

inputs.name: Bending Arc
inputs.info: Arc defining the start, length, and angles of the bending portion of the deformation.

components.author: DavidR
components.name: Cage Between Edges
components.info: Create a twisted box cage between four edges.

inputs.name: Front Left Edge
inputs.info: Edge in cage W direction at $(u,v)$ = (0,0).

inputs.name: Front Right Edge
inputs.info: Edge in cage W direction at $(u,v)$ = (1,0)

inputs.name: Back Left Edge
inputs.info: Edge in cage W direction at $(u,v)$ = (0,1)

inputs.name: Back Right Edge
inputs.info: Edge in cage W direction at $(u,v)$ = (1,1)

inputs.name: Degree U
inputs.info: Degree in cage U direction, between 1 and 7.

inputs.name: Degree V
inputs.info: Degree in cage V direction, between 1 and 7.

inputs.name: Degree W
inputs.info: Degree in cage W direction, between 1 and 7.

components.author: DavidR
components.name: Cage Between Faces
components.info: Create a twisted box cage between two surfaces.

inputs.name: Bottom
inputs.info: Surface for bottom face of cage.

inputs.name: Top
inputs.info: Surface for top face of cage.

inputs.name: Degree U
inputs.info: Degree in cage U direction, between 1 and 7.

inputs.name: Degree V
inputs.info: Degree in cage V direction, between 1 and 7.

inputs.name: Degree W
inputs.info: Degree in cage W direction, between 1 and 7.

components.author: DavidR
components.name: Cage Deform
components.info: Create a cage deformation. If an input shape is provided, it will be deformed accordingly.

inputs.name: Source
inputs.info: Simple box representing the initial form.

inputs.name: Target
inputs.info: Twisted cage representing the final form.

components.author: DanP
components.name: Cage From Surface
components.info: Create a deformation cage on a single-face surface.

inputs.name: U Interval
inputs.info: U interval for the subsurface to create the cage on.

inputs.name: V Interval
inputs.info: V interval for the subsurface to create the cage on.

inputs.name: Degree U
inputs.info: Degree in cage U direction, between 1 and 7.

inputs.name: Degree V
inputs.info: Degree in cage V direction, between 1 and 7.

inputs.name: Degree W
inputs.info: Degree in cage W direction, between 1 and 7.

components.author: DavidR
components.name: Change Of Basis
components.info: Create a transformation from one oblique coordinate system into another.

inputs.name: Source Origin
inputs.info: Point of origin of the source coordinate system.

inputs.name: Source X
inputs.info: X unit vector of the source coordinate system.

inputs.name: Source Y
inputs.info: Y unit vector of the source coordinate system.

inputs.name: Source Z
inputs.info: Z unit vector of the source coordinate system.

inputs.name: Target Origin
inputs.info: Point of origin of the target coordinate system.

inputs.name: Target X
inputs.info: X unit vector of the target coordinate system.

inputs.name: Target Y
inputs.info: Y unit vector of the target coordinate system.

inputs.name: Target Z
inputs.info: Z unit vector of the target coordinate system.

components.author: DavidR
components.name: Combine Deform
components.info: Combine two non-linear spatial deformations.

components.author: DavidR
components.name: Curl Deform
components.info: Create a curling deformation. Curling is similar to wringing, but with a curved axis. If an input shape is provided, it will be deformed accordingly.

inputs.name: Angle
inputs.info: Either a global angle, or a function which defines a unique angle for every parameter along the axis curve.

inputs.name: Degrees
inputs.info: If true, function values are interpreted to represent angular degrees. If false, it is assumed to be in radians.

components.author: DavidR
components.name: Mirror In Curve
components.info: Create a curve mirror deformation. If an input shape is provided, it will be deformed accordingly.

inputs.name: Shape
inputs.info: Optional shape to mirror in the curve.

inputs.name: Infinite
inputs.info: If true, open mirror curves are extended linearly at both ends.

components.author: DavidR
components.name: Evaluate Cage
components.info: Evaluate a cage at normalised (u,v,w) parameters.

inputs.name: U Parameter
inputs.info: Normalised parameter in the cage U direction.

inputs.name: V Parameter
inputs.info: Normalised parameter in the cage V direction.

inputs.name: W Parameter
inputs.info: Normalised parameter in the cage W direction.

components.author: DavidR
components.name: Expand Deform
components.info: Create an expansion deformation. If an input shape is provided, it will be deformed accordingly.

inputs.name: Seed
inputs.info: Seed from which expansion is measured. May be a point, a plane, an infinite line, or a curve.

inputs.name: Factor
inputs.info: Function encoding the scaling factor based on the distance to the seed. Ideally this function is strictly increasing.

components.author: DavidR
components.name: Field Deform
components.info: Create a vector field deformation. If an input shape is provided, it will be deformed accordingly.

inputs.name: Motion
inputs.info: Optional magnitude of particle motion through the field.

components.author: DavidR
components.name: Flow Along Curve
components.info: Create a deformation from one axial curve to another. If an input shape is provided, it will be deformed accordingly.

inputs.name: Source
inputs.info: Optional source curve. If omitted, a line tangent with the start of the target curve is used.

inputs.name: R Factor
inputs.info: Scaling factor radial to the target curve.

components.author: DavidR
components.name: Flow Along Surface
components.info: Create a flow deformation which maps onto a surface UVW space. If an input shape is provided, it will be deformed accordingly.

inputs.name: Source
inputs.info: Source space in the form of a rectilinear box.

inputs.name: U Domain
inputs.info: Optional U domain for target space. If omitted, the entire domain will be used.

inputs.name: V Domain
inputs.info: Optional V domain for target space. If omitted, the entire domain will be used.

inputs.name: W Factor
inputs.info: Scaling factor in the surface normal direction.

components.author: DanPiker
components.name: Maelstrom Deform
components.info: Create a spiral deformation. If an input shape is provided, it will be deformed accordingly.

components.author: DavidR
components.name: Offset Deform
components.info: Create an offset deformation. If an input shape is provided, it will be deformed accordingly.

inputs.name: Seed
inputs.info: Seed from which the offset is measured. May be a point, a plane, an infinite line, or a curve.

inputs.name: Factor
inputs.info: Function encoding the offset amount based on the distance to the seed. Ideally the function intersects $(0,0)$.

components.author: DavidR
components.name: Splop Deform
components.info: Create a splop deformation which maps from flat space into surface UVW space. If an input shape is provided, it will be deformed accordingly.

inputs.name: Locus
inputs.info: Surface locus where the deformation origin is anchored.

components.author: DavidR
components.name: Sporph Deform
components.info: Create a sporph deformation which maps between surface UVW spaces. If an input shape is provided, it will be deformed accordingly.

inputs.name: Source
inputs.info: Reference source surface for sporph deformation.

components.author: DavidR
components.name: Stretch Deform
components.info: Create a stretching deformation. If an input shape is provided, it will be deformed accordingly.

inputs.name: Line
inputs.info: Line covering the region to be stretched.

inputs.name: Length
inputs.info: Length of stretched line, as measured from the fixed start.

components.author: DavidR
components.name: Mirror In Surface
components.info: Create a surface mirror deformation. If an input shape is provided, it will be deformed accordingly.

inputs.name: Shape
inputs.info: Optional shape to mirror in the surface.

inputs.name: Infinite
inputs.info: If true, the reflection occurs in the tangent plane at the closest point on the surface.

components.author: DanPiker
components.name: Taper Deform
components.info: Create a tapering deformation. If an input shape is provided, it will be deformed accordingly.

inputs.name: Start Radius
inputs.info: Radius at the start of the taper axis.

inputs.name: End Radius
inputs.info: Radius at the end of the taper axis.

inputs.name: Infinite
inputs.info: If true, the taper deformation extends infinitely beyond the limits of the axis.

components.author: DavidR
components.name: Twist Deform
components.info: Create a twisting deformation. If an input shape is provided, it will be deformed accordingly.

inputs.name: Angle 1
inputs.info: Rotational angle at the start of the axis.

inputs.name: Angle 2
inputs.info: Rotational angle at the end of the axis.

inputs.name: Profile
inputs.info: Progression of the twist along the axis.

components.author: DavidR
components.name: Twist Deform
components.info: Create a twisting deformation. If an input shape is provided, it will be deformed accordingly.

inputs.name: Angle 1
inputs.info: Rotational angle at the start of the axis.

inputs.name: Angle 2
inputs.info: Rotational angle at the end of the axis.

components.author: DavidR
components.name: Wring Deform
components.info: Create a wringing deformation. Wringing is similar to twisting, but with a variable angle progression. If an input shape is provided, it will be deformed accordingly.

inputs.name: Plane
inputs.info: Orientation plane. The wringing axis is coincident with the plane z-axis.

inputs.name: Angle
inputs.info: Function describing the wringing angle based on distance to plane.

inputs.name: Degrees
inputs.info: If true, the function values represent angles measured in degrees instead of radians.

components.author: DavidR
components.name: Carve Region
components.info: Carve a region into parallel slices using points.

components.author: DavidR
components.name: Curve Boolean
components.info: Find regions bounded by curves.

inputs.name: Points
inputs.info: Optional region seed points. If omitted, all regions will be found.

outputs.name: Regions
outputs.info: Regions based on curve boundaries and seed points.

outputs.name: Curve Map
outputs.info: List of curve indices contributing to each region.

outputs.name: Point Map
outputs.info: List of point indices contributing to each region.

components.author: DavidR
components.name: Sphere Section
components.info: Find the intersection circle between a plane and a sphere.

outputs.name: Circle
outputs.info: Circle at the intersection of the sphere and the plane.

components.author: DavidR
components.name: Sphere-Sphere
components.info: Find the circular intersection of two spheres.

outputs.name: Circle
outputs.info: Circle defined by the intersection of two spheres.

components.author: DavidR
components.name: Arc-Arc
components.info: Find the intersection points of two circular arcs.

outputs.name: Parameter A
outputs.info: Parameter of the first intersection on arc 1.

outputs.name: Paramerer B
outputs.info: Parameter of the second intersection on arc 1.

components.author: DavidR
components.name: Box Section
components.info: Find the intersection polyline between a plane and a box.

components.author: DavidR
components.name: Collide List
components.info: Find collisions between all the shapes in a list.

inputs.name: Tolerance
inputs.info: Optional distance tolerance for collision detection. If omitted, the Absolute Tolerance Pin is used as a fallback.

outputs.name: Collision
outputs.info: True if the collider is within the tolerance distance of any of the other shapes.

outputs.name: Indices
outputs.info: Indices of all colliding obstacles per shape.

components.author: DavidR
components.name: Collide With Shapes
components.info: Find collisions between an object and a list of obstacles.

inputs.name: Tolerance
inputs.info: Optional distance tolerance for collision detection. Positive tolerances also count near misses as collisions, negative tolerances only count overlaps deeper than the tolerance. Since only closed shapes can overlap, negative tolerances never yield collisions between points, curves or open surfaces. If omitted, the Absolute Tolerance Pin is used as a fallback.

outputs.name: Collision
outputs.info: True if the collider is within the tolerance distance of any of the obstacles.

outputs.name: Indices
outputs.info: Indices of all obstacles that collide with the shape.

components.author: DavidR
components.name: Curve Contours
components.info: Create a set of equally spaced curve contour points.

outputs.name: Loci
outputs.info: Loci of contour points on the curve.

outputs.name: Layer
outputs.info: Layer, i.e. contour section offset, given as an integer. Layer zero is the section through the base point.

components.author: DavidR
components.name: Curve-Curve
components.info: Find the intersection points between two curves.

outputs.name: First Loci
outputs.info: Loci of all intersections on the first curve.

outputs.name: Second Loci
outputs.info: Loci of all intersections on the second curve.

components.author: DavidR
components.name: Curve-Line
components.info: Find the intersection points of a curve and an infinite line.

components.author: DavidR
components.name: Curve Section
components.info: Find the intersection points of a curve and a plane.

components.author: DavidR
components.name: Curve-Self
components.info: Find the self-intersections of a curve.

outputs.name: Loci
outputs.info: Loci of all intersections on the curve.

components.author: DavidR
components.name: Curve-Surface
components.info: Find the intersection points between a curve and a surface.

outputs.name: Curve Loci
outputs.info: Loci of all intersections on the curve.

outputs.name: Surface Loci
outputs.info: Loci of all intersections on the surface.

components.author: DavidR
components.name: Curve-Surface
components.info: Find the intersection points and overlaps between a curve and a surface.

outputs.name: Curve Loci
outputs.info: Loci of all intersections on the curve.

outputs.name: Surface Loci
outputs.info: Loci of all intersections on the surface.

components.author: AndyP
components.name: Isovist 2D
components.info: Compute an isovist by casting sample rays radially around a plane.

inputs.name: Plane
inputs.info: Plane encoding the location and orientation of the observer.

inputs.name: Radius
inputs.info: Optional maximum sampling radius. If omitted, the largest meaningful radius is picked and all hit-less rays are omitted from the outputs.

inputs.name: Obstacles
inputs.info: Ray obstacles. May incluce curves, planes, surfaces, and meshes.

inputs.name: Mode
inputs.info: Ray casting accuracy. Accurate uses exact surface intersections; Fast meshes surfaces for speed.

outputs.name: Points
outputs.info: Point where each sample ray stops, either at an obstacle hit or at the horizon.

outputs.name: Rays
outputs.info: Ray vector from the origin to each sample point.

outputs.name: Distances
outputs.info: Distance from the origin to each sample point.

outputs.name: Indices
outputs.info: Index of the obstacle hit by each ray, or -1 if no obstacle was hit.

components.author: AndyP
components.name: Isovist 3D
components.info: Compute an isovist by casting sample rays spherically around a location.

inputs.name: Plane
inputs.info: Sampling plane and origin. For a hemisphere the plane is the horizon and rays are cast above it.

inputs.name: Obstacles
inputs.info: Obstacles to sample against (curves, planes, surfaces and meshes are supported).

inputs.name: Domain
inputs.info: Whether to sample the upper hemisphere or the full sphere of directions.

inputs.name: Mode
inputs.info: Ray casting accuracy. Accurate uses exact surface intersections; Fast meshes surfaces for speed.

outputs.name: Points
outputs.info: Point where each sample ray stops, either at an intersection or at the horizon.

outputs.name: Rays
outputs.info: Ray vector from the origin to each sample point.

outputs.name: Distances
outputs.info: Distance from the origin to each sample point.

outputs.name: Indices
outputs.info: Index of the obstacle hit by each ray, or -1 if no obstacle was hit.

components.author: DavidR
components.name: Isovist Coverage
components.info: Compute coverage and visibility statistics for a collection of isovist rays.

inputs.name: Rays
inputs.info: Isovist rays. Use the Rays output of an Isovist 2D or Isovist 3D component.

outputs.name: Coverage
outputs.info: Fraction of the original sampling dome occupied by rays that hit an obstacle.

outputs.name: Hits
outputs.info: Number of rays that hit an obstacle.

outputs.name: Mininum Distance
outputs.info: Smallest visible distance among hit rays, or zero if there were no hits.

outputs.name: Mean Distance
outputs.info: Average visible distance among hit rays, or zero if there were no hits.

outputs.name: Maximum Distance
outputs.info: Largest visible distance among hit rays, or zero if there were no hits.

outputs.name: Distance Deviation
outputs.info: Standard deviation of visible distance among hit rays, or zero if there were no hits.

components.author: DavidR
components.name: Isovist Extent
components.info: Compute the area (2D) or volume (3D) of an isovist, optionally with a distance falloff.

inputs.name: Rays
inputs.info: Isovist rays. Use the Rays output of an Isovist 2D or Isovist 3D component.

inputs.name: Weight
inputs.info: Distance falloff applied to each ray's contribution.

inputs.name: Transition
inputs.info: Transition distance where the falloff begins to take effect. Ignored for Block.

inputs.name: Normalise
inputs.info: If true, divide by the maximum possible extent at the sample horizon so the result is a unitless score. If false, report the absolute area or volume metrics.

outputs.name: Extent
outputs.info: Isovist area (2D) or volume (3D). With Normalise on, a unitless openness score in $[0,1]$; otherwise an absolute measure.

components.author: AndyP
components.name: Isovist Field 2D
components.info: Create a scalar field whose value at each point is a planar isovist statistic.

inputs.name: Plane
inputs.info: Orientation of the sampling planes. The isovist at each queried point is cast on a plane parallel to this.

inputs.name: Count
inputs.info: Number of sample rays per isovist. Lower values evaluate faster when the field is sampled densely.

inputs.name: Obstacles
inputs.info: Obstacles to sample against (curves, planes, surfaces and meshes are supported).

inputs.name: Metric
inputs.info: Scalar metric reported at each query point.

inputs.name: Transition
inputs.info: Transition distance where the falloff begins. Ignored unless the metric is LinearRamp, Exponential or Smoothstep (or their normalised variants).

outputs.name: Field
outputs.info: Scalar field of the selected isovist metric at each point.

components.author: AndyP
components.name: Isovist Field 3D
components.info: Create a scalar field whose value at each point is a spherical isovist statistic.

inputs.name: Plane
